strategy: Start with a short, near-limit memory test on the single-replica catalog service because it reaches every flow and may reveal OOM behavior that the earlier 64 MB test did not. Then test a brief currency-service outage for error blast radius, a moderate recommendation-service delay below the guard threshold, and a recommendation-service pod kill to measure recovery without repeating well-known high-impact tests.

spec.reason: Ranked first because productcatalogservice is single-replica, has a 128 Mi memory limit, and reaches all five user flows. The earlier 64 MB stress run had no user-visible impact, while 110 MB tests near-limit behavior; cartservice with the same 128 Mi limit OOMed under 110 MB stress.
spec.hypothesis: Near-limit allocation may OOM or destabilize productcatalogservice, causing broad errors and severe latency until the guard removes the fault.

experiments.learning_goal: Does productcatalogservice tolerate near-limit memory pressure, or does it OOM and disrupt the shop before the fault is removed?

spec.reason: currencyservice is a single replica and a shared dependency of frontend and checkoutservice, reaching home, product, view_cart, and checkout. Its latency and packet-loss behavior have been tested, but an outright short outage has not; the short duration bounds this error-class blast-radius test.
spec.hypothesis: Taking currencyservice unavailable will cause errors in flows that need currency conversion; the broad reach makes a guard abort plausible, while failed RPCs may fail fast rather than create sustained slowdown.

experiments.learning_goal: Which user flows fail when the shared currency dependency is unavailable, and does the safety guard stop the outage promptly?

spec.reason: recommendationservice is single-replica and reaches product, view_cart, and checkout. Its earlier 40 ms delay attempt was aborted before injection, leaving its slowdown sensitivity unmeasured; 30 ms with modest jitter is a bounded probe, unlike the documented 100 ms catalog delay that drove all flows to roughly 700 ms.
spec.hypothesis: Added latency will slow flows that call recommendationservice, particularly product, without causing errors or approaching the 1500 ms guard limit.

experiments.learning_goal: How much does a modest recommendation-service delay propagate to its dependent user flows?

spec.reason: recommendationservice has one replica and reaches three flows, making it a useful recovery probe with a narrower expected blast radius than the all-flow entrypoint or shared cart dependency. A prior productcatalogservice kill coincided with a recommendationservice restart, but there is no direct recommendationservice kill run measuring its own replacement and user impact.
spec.hypothesis: Kubernetes should replace the killed pod; callers may see brief errors or latency while it restarts, then recover without a sustained guard breach.

experiments.learning_goal: How quickly does recommendationservice recover after pod loss, and do its callers experience a noticeable interruption?

skipped_ideas.idea: Repeat a 100 ms network delay on productcatalogservice.
skipped_ideas.why_not: Multiple completed runs already show severe slowdown across all five flows, with p95 around 718–757 ms; this would repeat a well-established result.

skipped_ideas.idea: Repeat a 300-user traffic spike on frontend.
skipped_ideas.why_not: Repeated runs already approach or cross the 1500 ms guard threshold with broad slowdown, so another run would add little overall-resilience insight.
A prior run already tripped the p95 guard at 1571 ms after only 6.6 seconds, establishing a severe shared-dependency slowdown; the selected tests cover unmeasured behavior instead.
